hypothesis: Split-KV (flash-decoding) path for non-causal launches whose base grid underfills the GPU: partition the KV sequence across splits so total CTAs ~4x SM count, each split writes a normalized fp32 partial output plus LSE to a workspace, and a second Triton kernel combines splits with log-sum-exp weights.
rationale: Decode launches only cdiv(1,16)*32*1 = 32 CTAs on a 170-SM card, so >80% of SMs idle while each CTA streams the entire KV sequence serially; decode is memory-bound and needs many loads in flight across all SMs. Baseline decode rows are 3-7.5x slower than FA2 (worst row 0.13x), dominating the geomean loss. Prefill path is untouched.
expected_effect: Decode rows speed up several-fold (largest gains at long seq_kv, e.g. decode_65536 from 1.39 ms toward ~0.2-0.3 ms); prefill unchanged; geomean rises substantially (roughly 0.27 -> 0.45+).
